Calculate extended BMI measures

Source: R/cdc.R
ext_bmiz.Rd

ext_bmiz Calculates the sigma (scale parameter for the half-normal distribution), extended BMI percentile, extended BMIz, and the CDC LMS Z-scores for weight, height, and BMI for children between 2 and 19.9 years of age. Note that for BMIs <= 95th percentile of the CDC growth charts, the extended values for BMI are equal to the LMS values. The extended values differ only for children who have a BMI > 95th percentile.

Usage

ext_bmiz(
  data,
  age = "agem",
  wt = "wt",
  ht = "ht",
  bmi = "bmi",
  adjust.integer.age = TRUE,
  ref.data.path = ""
)

Arguments

data

Input data frame or data table

age

Name of input column containing subject age in months in quotes, default "agem"

wt

Name of input column containing weight (kg) value in quotes, default "wt"

ht

Name of input column containing height (cm) value in quotes, default "ht"

bmi

Name of input column containing calculated BMI in quotes, default "bmi"

adjust.integer.age

If age inputs are all integer, add 0.5 if TRUE; default TRUE

ref.data.path

Path to directory containing reference data

Value

A data.table: a copy of data (same rows, row order, column names, and values) with these columns added: bmiz, bmip, waz, wp, haz, hp, p95, p97, bmip95, mod_bmiz, mod_waz, mod_haz, sigma, original_bmip, original_bmiz, sev_obese, obese.

Details

This function produces output equivalent to CDC software and the cdcanthro R package.

The extended BMIz is the inverse cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the extended BMI percentile. If the extended percentile is very close to 100, the qnorm function in R produces an infinite value. This occurs only if the extended BMI percentile is > 99.99999999999999. This occurs infrequently, such as a 48-month-old with a BMI > 39, and it is likely that these BMIs represent data entry errors. For these cases, extended BMIz is set to 8.21, a value that is slightly greater than the largest value that can be calculated.

The output columns are listed under Value below.

data must have columns for at least age, sex, weight, height, and bmi.

age should be coded in months, using the most precise values available. To convert to months from age in years, multiply by 12. To convert to months from age in days, divide by 30.4375 (365.25 / 12).

sex: we recommend M and F, which is what longwide() returns. Male can be coded as boy, Boy, b, B, male, Male, m, or M, and female can be coded as girl, Girl, g, G, female, Female, f, or F. Numeric sex is accepted only if sex has both 1s and 2s and no other values, read as 1 = male, 2 = female; otherwise ext_bmiz() stops. This is because 0/1 is the numeric coding in cleangrowth(), and a column of only 1s could be either coding. The 1/2 coding matches the CDC reference data, CDC software, and the cdcanthro package. Other text values, and logical values, are not recognized: their z-scores are NA, with a warning.

wt should be in kilograms.

ht should be in centimeters.

Specify the input data column names for age, wt, ht, bmi using quotation marks. See example below.

ext_bmiz() does not change data. It returns a copy of data with the new columns added; your column names and values are kept as they are (the 0.5 added by adjust.integer.age is used only in the calculation). If data already has a column with the name of one of the columns ext_bmiz() adds (bmiz, bmip, waz, wp, haz, hp, p95, p97, bmip95, mod_bmiz, mod_waz, mod_haz, sigma, original_bmip, original_bmiz, sev_obese, obese), for example from an earlier run, it warns and the returned data has the newly calculated values in that column; rename the column first to keep both.

Values are calculated for ages 24 through 240 months, as in the cdcanthro package. Age 730 days is 23.98 months (730 / 30.4375), which is below 24 months, so a row at 730 days has NA values even though a child at that age may be exactly 2 years old; values begin at 731 days. A warning gives the number of rows at about 729-730 days.

If the argument adjust.integer.age is TRUE (the default), 0.5 will be added to all age values for the calculation if all input values are integers. Set to FALSE to disable.

By default, the reference data file CDCref_d.csv, made available at https://www.cdc.gov/growth-chart-training/hcp/computer-programs/index.html, is included in this package for convenience. If you are developing this package, use ref.data.path to adjust the path to this file from your working directory if necessary.

References

Wei R, Ogden CL, Parsons VL, Freedman DS, Hales CM. A method for calculating BMI z-scores and percentiles above the 95th percentile of the CDC growth charts. Ann Hum Biol. 2020 Sep;47(6):514-521. doi:10.1080/03014460.2020.1808065 .

Examples

# \donttest{
# Run on a small subset of given data
df <- as.data.frame(syngrowth)
df <- df[df$subjid %in% unique(df[, "subjid"])[1:5], ]
# cleangrowth() returns the data with an 'exclude' column
clean_df <- cleangrowth(df)
#> [14:12:07] growthcleanr: cleaning in progress — 5 subjects, 93 measurements, 1 batch of up to 5,000 subjects
#> ************************************************************
#> growthcleanr cleaning summary  (93 measurements)
#>   Weight      : 45 included (80.4%), 11 excluded (19.6%)
#>   Height      : 32 included (86.5%), 5 excluded (13.5%)
#>   Set aside   : 0 (0.0%)
#> ************************************************************
df_wide <- longwide(clean_df) # convert to wide format for ext_bmiz
df_wide_bmi <- simple_bmi(df_wide) # compute simple BMI

# Calling the function with default column names
df_bmiz <- ext_bmiz(df_wide_bmi)

# Specifying different column names; note that quotes are used
dfc <- simple_bmi(df_wide)
colnames(dfc)[colnames(dfc) %in% c("agem", "wt", "ht")] <-
  c("agemos", "weightkg", "heightcm")
df_bmiz <- ext_bmiz(dfc, age="agemos", wt="weightkg", ht="heightcm")

# Disabling conversion of all-integer age in months to (age + 0.5)
dfc <- simple_bmi(df_wide)
df_bmiz <- ext_bmiz(dfc, adjust.integer.age=FALSE)
# }
